Performers
Sergei Rachmaninoff (piano), Philadelphia Orchestra (orchestra), Leopold Stokowski (conductor) Documented

The HMV label uses Philadelphia Symphony Orchestra; DAHR identifies the ensemble as the Philadelphia Orchestra.

[2] [3]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The performing edition is not identified. This file is the complete transfer of the slow movement’s first original side, part 4 of the concerto’s disc sequence. It omits the subsequent sides, including the later central section, cadenza and return; no sides have been joined.

[1] [3]
Recorded
10 April 1929 Documented

DAHR identifies take 1 as the issued master. The Archive’s November 1929 date describes the HMV issue, not the recording session.

[3]
Place
Academy of Music, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania Documented

The matrix’s Take Date and Place table names the Academy of Music. Camden in the issue’s MARC publisher imprint is not adopted as a recording venue.

[3]
Label
His Master’s Voice / The Gramophone Co. Ltd. Documented

UK 12-inch 78-rpm pressing, manufactured at Hayes, Middlesex, England according to the label.

[2] [1]
Catalogue
D.B. 1334 Documented

The label marks the side No. 4 and 2nd Movement–Adagio sostenuto (1st Record). The other face contains the first movement’s third side. Internet Archive dates the HMV issue to November 1929; DAHR’s generated MARC imprint gives [1929].

[2] [4] [1]
Matrix, take, sides
Victor CVE-48966, take 1; Gramophone face number 2-05744; concerto part 4 Documented

DAHR connects the master take to DB-1334 and distinguishes 2-05744 as a Gramophone face number. The Archive transcribes A48966 as another disc identifier; it is not treated as a separate performance or take.

[2] [1] [3] [4]
Transfer
Phoebe Pugh, transfer and metadata; Akin Gaddis, disc cleaning; George Blood, L.P., digitisation Documented

Credits are the Archive’s user_transferred, user_metadataentered, user_cleaned and scanningcenter fields. The carrier belongs to the Leif Druedahl collection.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item was made public on 20 April 2023; this is an upload date, not a documented transfer date.

[1]
Processing
Digitised at 78 rpm; preferred 3.3-mil truncated-conical stylus transfer, equalised with turnover 500.0; 24-bit FLAC master and VBR MP3 access derivative. Documented

The Archive documents four stylus transfers and identifies the chosen stylus in the preferred FLAC comment. No additional restoration or speed correction has been applied for this edition. Surface noise limits automatic onset and pitch-class estimates; these are not treated as counts of played notes or verified changes of key.

[1]
Composition rights
Public domain in ordinary life-plus-70 jurisdictions. Inferred, not documented

Rachmaninoff died on 28 March 1943. This concerns the composition, not the separately assessed recording, transfer or an unidentified modern edition.

[5] [6]
Recording rights
Territorial EU public-domain basis: sound recording published before 1963. Documented

Rule 3. Internet Archive dates HMV DB-1334 to November 1929, and DAHR’s issue record supplies a [1929] publication imprint and the link to CVE-48966 take 1. The former 50-year recording term expired before the 2013 extension, which applies to recordings still protected on 1 November 2013. US public-domain status is not established. This independent George Blood transfer has no licenceurl or non-commercial condition in the consulted item metadata and identifies its own original FLAC and physical carrier. F. Reeder’s separate RACHMANINOFFPianoConcertoNo.2InCMinor-NEWTRANSFER carries CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 and is expressly excluded, not an upstream source for this audio. This is a territorial recording-term assessment, not a worldwide licence or a claim that the modern transfer has been freely licensed.

Sergei Rachmaninoff, piano; Philadelphia Orchestra; Leopold Stokowski, conductor. Recorded 10 April 1929. HMV D.B. 1334, Adagio opening side only; Leif Druedahl collection, digitised by George Blood, L.P., via Internet Archive. Territorial EU public-domain recording basis; US status not established.
